disposition_mapping.rationale: The calendar and central assumptions issuance is preserved but restructured to publish the downside macro scenario as a selectable, system-modelled variant rather than a static document, satisfying ABB-R-01 and ABB-R-10.
Top-down target setting is unconstrained by design and is retained substantially unchanged, now published directly into the planning platform as guardrails for bottom-up submissions.
Revenue and volume planning is preserved per ABB-R-02 but restructured into driver-based templates with in-line validation against the downside scenario, improving quality without changing ownership.
Cost centre and headcount budgeting is preserved per ABB-R-03 but restructured into standardised templates with automated deviation flagging against top-down targets.
Capex request submission persists but is restructured to enforce the business-case requirement above threshold at point of submission, continuing to consume the business case input per ABB-R-04.

Consolidation into the draft three-statement budget survives per ABB-R-06 and is restructured into an automated process that still consumes accounting policies applied to actuals (ABB-R-05, KB-06 policy consistency) and central FX assumptions (ABB-R-07, KB-07 FX translation), adding an automated reconciliation check to strengthen the evidential trail (KB-02).

Review and challenge is unconstrained by design and is restructured into a platform-supported continuous cycle with live scenario drill-down, reducing iteration count while preserving the challenge function.
Board approval survives per ABB-R-11, retained substantially unchanged but with an auditable digital approval record, and continues to precede load-and-lock per ABB-R-08.

Loading and locking of the approved version survives per ABB-R-09, restructured to use role-based system controls that enforce the lock only after board approval is confirmed, preserving the ordering required by ABB-R-08 and the period-cutoff discipline in KB-03.

steps.description: FP&A issues the budget calendar and a central assumptions pack (inflation, FX, interest rates) through the planning platform, including at least one downside macro scenario modelled as a selectable variant so submitters can stress-test plans against it from day one.
steps.name: Issue calendar, central assumptions and scenario set

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets, informed by the strategic plan and the central assumptions pack, and publish them into the planning platform as binding guardrails for bottom-up submissions.
steps.name: Set top-down targets

steps.description: Business unit heads prepare and own revenue and volume plans using driver-based templates pre-loaded with top-down targets and central assumptions, with in-line validation against the downside scenario variant.
steps.name: Revenue and volume plans (driver-based)

steps.description: Cost centre owners prepare and own cost centre and headcount budgets using standardised templates that enforce the central assumptions and flag deviations from top-down targets automatically.
steps.name: Cost centre and headcount budgets (template-driven)

steps.description: Business unit heads submit capex requests through the planning platform; any request above the threshold is blocked from submission until a business case is attached, enforcing the control at source rather than in later review.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests with business case

steps.description: The planning platform automatically consolidates revenue, cost, headcount and capex submissions into a draft P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, applying the same accounting policies used for actuals and the central FX assumptions for translation, and runs an automated three-statement reconciliation check before releasing the draft for review.
steps.name: Automated consolidation into draft three-statement budget

steps.description: FP&A and the CFO run a structured, platform-supported review and challenge cycle with submitters, using live drill-down into drivers and the downside scenario variant to converge on a revised budget in fewer, shorter iterations than the prior email-based cycle.
steps.name: Continuous review and challenge cycle

steps.description: The board reviews the revised budget, including the downside scenario view, and formally approves it, with the approval decision and supporting pack captured in an auditable digital record.
steps.name: Board approval

steps.description: The board-approved budget is loaded into the planning and reporting systems and locked via role-based access control as the single version used for variance analysis, with the lock enforced only after board approval is confirmed in the system.
steps.name: Load and lock approved budget version
